topic_brief.title: No-till vs conventional tillage effects on crop yield
topic_brief.research_question: Does no-till management affect crop yield compared to conventional tillage, and how does this vary by crop type and climate?
topic_brief.intervention_description: No-till or zero-till management (seeds planted directly into undisturbed soil)
topic_brief.comparator_description: Conventional tillage (moldboard plow, disk, chisel, or other inversion/intensive tillage)
topic_brief.outcome_description: Crop grain yield per unit area
important_moderators: Crop species (wheat, maize, rice, soybean, barley, sorghum, cotton, etc.)
Soil type or texture (clay, loam, sand)
topic_brief.benchmark_notes: Overall -5.7%; Wheat -2.6%; Maize -7.6%; Rice -7.5%; Soybean +0.3%; Oilseed rape -9.0%

rows.title: Long-term analysis of soil water conservation and crop yield under different tillage systems in Mediterranean rainfed conditions
rows.treatment_description: No-tillage (NT), direct seeding without soil disturbance
rows.control_description: Mouldboard plough (Mb), 30-35 cm depth + 1-2 cultivator passes at 15 cm
rows.notes: Significant tillage effect on yield (P<0.0001). NT ranked 'a', Mb ranked 'c' by LSD(0.05). SD values are temporal (across 19 years), not within-year spatial variability. Mean averaged over all years and replicates (4 blocks). Agramunt is the driest site (highest water deficit). Yield ranking: NT > Sub-50 > Ch = Mb. Mb had lowest yields especially in dry years (<2000 kg/ha). TIL*YEAR interaction significant (P<0.0001).

moderators.mod_residue_management: retained (straw chopped and spread by combine)
